mainTopic: Plowing before שביעית, and watering fields on חול המועד
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא learns from a פסוק that plowing before שביעית is forbidden, while רבי ישמעאל reads the same פסוק as being about שבת. After trying another answer, the גמרא concludes that for רבי ישמעאל the ban comes from a הלכה למשה מסיני, and for רבי עקיבא it comes from the פסוקים. רבי יוחנן says רבן גמליאל ובית דינו cancelled the ban using a גזירה שוה from שבת בראשית. רב אשי objects that a גזירה שוה cannot uproot a הלכה or a פסוק. He explains instead that the הלכה applied only while the בית המקדש stood. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's ban on watering fields with rainwater on חול המועד. It explains the ban, and it discusses streams, pools, channels and dripping water, all based on one question: will the water run out and lead to hard work? Two ברייתות forbid lifting water from a lower garden bed to a higher one, and allow watering vegetables in order to eat them. The amud ends with a story in which רבה תוספאה starts to explain that the word מדלין does not mean drawing water. His explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי עקיבא's reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי עקיבא's teaching. The פסוק forbids plowing before שביעית that carries into שביעית, and reaping שביעית crops that carry over into the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: …plowing that enters into the seventh year, and reaping of the seventh year that goes out into the year after the seventh.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that was already being quoted. רבי עקיבא explains that the פסוק is about work done at the edges of שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says the פסוק does not need to teach that plowing and reaping in שביעית itself are forbidden, since that is already known. So it must be adding two new cases. The first is plowing in the sixth year that helps the crop of שביעית. The second is reaping, in the eighth year, a crop that grew during שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, when working the land is forbidden
The year right after שביעית (the eighth year)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא here is not about plowing during שביעית itself. It is about plowing before it that helps the שביעית crop, and reaping after it.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because רבי עקיבא gets this ban from a פסוק, the גמרא will need to explain what the הלכה למשה מסיני adds.

phrases.english: [plowing of the sixth year] that enters into the seventh year,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence. The ברייתא is explaining the פסוק 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות' (שמות 34:21).

phrases.english: and reaping of the seventh year
that goes out into the year after the seventh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the פסוק forbids plowing before שביעית that helps the שביעית crop, and reaping in the eighth year of a crop that grew in שביעית.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל reads the verse as being about שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל compares reaping to plowing. Only optional reaping is forbidden on שבת, so reaping the עומר, which is a מצוה, is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: just as plowing is optional, so too the reaping meant here is optional reaping. This leaves out reaping the עומר, which is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second opinion on the same פסוק. רבי ישמעאל uses it to talk about שבת, not שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing is never a מצוה, so it is always 'optional' work. Since reaping is placed next to plowing, רבי ישמעאל learns that only optional reaping is forbidden on שבת. That means the מצוה of reaping the עומר may be done even on שבת. For him, this פסוק says nothing about the time before שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: Reaping the barley for the עומר offering
'Just as… so too…': a way of comparing two things

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל is not arguing about the law of plowing before שביעית here. He just uses this פסוק for something else, about שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
just as plowing is optional,
so too, reaping [that is forbidden] is optional,
this leaves out reaping the omer,
which is a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק, unlike רבי עקיבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only optional reaping is forbidden on שבת, so reaping the עומר is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns the ban on plowing before שביעית from the פסוק. רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק for שבת. So for רבי עקיבא, the גמרא must still explain why the הלכה למשה מסיני is needed.

steps.title: The הלכה permits young saplings; the verses forbid old trees
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new answer. The הלכה למשה מסיני is a leniency for young saplings. The פסוקים are where the ban on plowing around old trees comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: when we learned the הלכה, it was to permit young saplings. The verses are there to forbid old trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops an earlier answer. רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new way to explain why both a פסוק and a הלכה למשה מסיני are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי עקיבא already has a פסוק forbidding plowing before שביעית, so the הלכה seems extra. רב נחמן בר יצחק splits the jobs. The פסוקים forbid plowing around old trees, and the הלכה allows plowing around young saplings. This way each source teaches something different.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': drops the earlier answer and gives a new one
'We learned it as a tradition': a הלכה למשה מסיני

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
when we learned the halakha [from Sinai],
it was to permit [plowing around] young saplings.
The verses are to forbid [plowing around] old trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why רבי עקיבא needs the הלכה if he already has the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources: each one teaches a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הלכה and the פסוק seem to teach the same ban, so one of them looks extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה permits young saplings, and the פסוקים forbid old trees.

steps.title: If young ones are permitted, aren't old ones automatically forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק. If the הלכה says young saplings are permitted, that already tells us old trees are forbidden. So why are the פסוקים needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the הלכה is there to permit young saplings, doesn't it follow on its own that old trees are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just heard. Step 5 answers this by dropping רב נחמן בר יצחק's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leniency for young saplings only makes sense if there is a ban on other trees. So the הלכה already shows that old trees are forbidden. That makes the פסוקים look extra again, and the original problem is back.

phrases.english: But since the halakha is to permit young saplings,
does it not follow automatically that an old tree is forbidden?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's split: the הלכה permits young saplings and the פסוקים forbid old trees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permitting young saplings already shows that old trees are forbidden. So the הלכה covers both cases, and the פסוקים are extra again.

steps.title: The הלכה is for רבי ישמעאל and the verses are for רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer. It says each source belongs to a different תנא: the הלכה למשה מסיני works for רבי ישמעאל, and the פסוקים work for רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the הלכה is the source according to רבי ישמעאל, and the פסוקים are the source according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of why we need both a הלכה and פסוקים. Its answer is that no single opinion needs both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as talking about שבת, which is why he needs the הלכה למשה מסיני for the ban on plowing before שביעית. רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק as talking about plowing before שביעית, so for him the פסוקים are the source. This means nothing is extra: each source belongs to a different view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the גמרא drops the old answer and gives a new one)
The הלכה למשה מסיני, a law passed down orally from משה at סיני

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on plowing before שביעית has two possible sources. For רבי ישמעאל it is a הלכה למשה מסיני; for רבי עקיבא it is the פסוקים.

phrases.english: Rather: the halacha is according to Rabbi Yishmael,
phrases.notes: רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק for שבת (step 2), so he needs the הלכה as the source for this ban.

phrases.english: the verses are according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by replacing רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the הלכה and the פסוקים seemed to belong to one view, so one of them looked unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה is the source for רבי ישמעאל and the פסוקים are the source for רבי עקיבא, so nothing is extra

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the cancellation was based on the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבן גמליאל ובית דינו cancelled the ban on working the land before שביעית, and they based it on the תורה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבן גמליאל and his court cancelled these bans based on the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion about how רבן גמליאל ובית דינו were able to cancel the ban on working before שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how a בית דין could cancel a law that comes from a הלכה or from a פסוק. רבי יוחנן's answer is that they did not overrule the תורה. They found a source in the תורה itself that allows the work. The next steps show what that source is.

keyTerms.meaning: רבן גמליאל and his court, who cancelled the extra time before שביעית
From the תורה; based on a תורה source

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabban Gamliel and his court
cancelled them based on the Torah.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the bans on working the land in the extra time before שביעית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new explanation of how רבן גמליאל ובית דינו could cancel the ban
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל ובית דינו cancelled the ban on working before שביעית based on a תורה source

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what תורה source רבי יוחנן is relying on.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source in the תורה rests behind רבי יוחנן's claim. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the cancellation was based on the תורה, but he did not say which source. The גמרא wants to see where it is written.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? What is the source?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יוחנן's statement in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תורה source allowed רבן גמליאל ובית דינו to cancel the ban

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from שבת בראשית
steps.stepSummary: The source is a גזירה שוה built on the word ״שבת״. On the weekly שבת, work is forbidden only on the day itself. So too, work is forbidden only during שביעית itself, not before it or after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the word ״שבת״ here and the word ״שבת״ by the שבת of Creation. Just as there, the day itself is forbidden but the days before and after it are allowed, so too here, the year itself is forbidden but the time before and after it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: רבי יוחנן's source is a גזירה שוה connecting שביעית to the weekly שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls שביעית a ״שבת״ for the land, and the weekly day of rest is also called ״שבת״. Nobody is forbidden to work on Friday or Sunday because of שבת. So the same must be true of שביעית, which means there is no ban on working the land in the time before it.

keyTerms.meaning: The שבת of Creation, meaning the weekly שבת
Just as there, so too here (the pattern of a comparison)

phrases.english: He learns "Shabbat"–"Shabbat" from the Shabbat of Creation.
phrases.notes: The first ״שבת״ is in the שביעית פסוק (ויקרא 25:4). It's a גזירה שוה: the same word in both places tells us they share a law.

phrases.english: Just as there, it itself is forbidden,
but before it and after it are permitted,
so too here, it itself is forbidden,
but before it and after it are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of ״שבת״ from the weekly שבת. Only the year itself is forbidden, and the time before it is permitted.

steps.title: רב אשי: can a גזירה שוה uproot a הלכה or a verse?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רבי יוחנן. The ban comes either from a הלכה למשה מסיני or from a פסוק, and in both cases a גזירה שוה should not be able to wipe it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: According to the one who says the ban is a הלכה, can a גזירה שוה come and uproot a הלכה? And according to the one who says it comes from a פסוק, can a גזירה שוה come and uproot a פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רבי יוחנן's explanation. He asks how a גזירה שוה could cancel something that has a solid source of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the ban comes from a הלכה (for רבי ישמעאל) or from פסוקים (for רבי עקיבא). A גזירה שוה is only a teaching method. It should not be strong enough to erase a clear law from סיני or a clear פסוק. So the challenge works whichever source you hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching method linking two places in the תורה that use the same word
The one who says (a certain opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the cancellation came from a גזירה שוה with שבת. רב אשי asks how a גזירה שוה could uproot a הלכה or a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly objected to it:
According to the one who says it is a halacha,
can a gezeira shava come and uproot a halacha?
And according to the one who says it is from a verse,
can a gezeira shava come and uproot a verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזירה שוה given in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim (steps 6 and 8) that a גזירה שוה allowed רבן גמליאל ובית דינו to cancel the ban
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban has its own strong source, a הלכה or a פסוק, and a גזירה שוה should not be able to uproot either one

steps.title: The rule from סיני only applied while the בית המקדש stood
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers his own question. רבן גמליאל ובית דינו follow רבי ישמעאל, and the הלכה למשה מסיני was given only for the time of the בית המקדש, like ניסוך המים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: רבן גמליאל and his court hold like רבי ישמעאל, who said the ban was learned as a הלכה from Sinai. But that הלכה was learned only for the time when the בית המקדש stands, like the water-pouring in the בית המקדש. When the בית המקדש does not stand, it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the problem he raised in step 9. A גזירה שוה cannot cancel a הלכה, but this הלכה was never meant to apply after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a גזירה שוה cannot override a הלכה למשה מסיני. רב אשי says nothing is being overridden: the הלכה was taught together with ניסוך המים, which is a בית המקדש practice, so it was only given for the time of the בית המקדש. Once the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן גמליאל ובית דינו could permit the work.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned it as a הלכה למשה מסיני (a law passed down from Sinai)
Pouring water on the מזבח on סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on working before שביעית was a הלכה that only applied while the בית המקדש stood. That is why רבן גמליאל ובית דינו could cancel it after the חורבן.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Rabban Gamliel and his court
hold like Rabbi Yishmael,
who said they learned it as a halacha.
phrases.notes: He means a הלכה למשה מסיני, and 'it' is the ban on working the land before שביעית.

phrases.english: And when they learned the halacha,
it was for the time when the Temple stands,
just like the water libation.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים —
phrases.english: But when the Temple is not standing,
it does not apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רב אשי's own challenge from step 9 by limiting the scope of the הלכה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the law: the הלכה was given only for the time of the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גזירה שוה was being used to cancel a הלכה למשה מסיני, which should be impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: No הלכה is cancelled. The הלכה never applied after the חורבן, so רבן גמליאל ובית דינו could permit the work.

steps.title: Why is rainwater forbidden if it takes no effort?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which forbids watering fields on חול המועד with rainwater or מי קילון. It accepts the reason for מי קילון but asks what effort is involved with rainwater.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but not with rainwater or with water drawn by a קילון. It makes sense for קילון water, because there is extra effort. But with rainwater, what effort is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about watering fields on חול המועד. It challenges why rainwater is on the forbidden list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hard work is not allowed on חול המועד. Lifting water with a קילון is hard work, so that ban makes sense. Rainwater already sits in a pit or cistern and can simply be channeled to the field, so the ban on it seems to have no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Rainwater collected in a pit or cistern
Water lifted with a קילון, a long pole with a bucket
It makes sense for (the first case), but (the second case is a problem)

phrases.english: But not with rainwater
or with water drawn by a shadoof.
phrases.notes: A קילון is a long pole with a bucket on one end, used to lift water up.

phrases.english: It makes sense for shadoof water,
since there is extra effort.
But with rainwater,
what effort is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מֵי קִילוֹן אִיכָּא טִירְחָא יַתִּירָא, אֶלָּא מֵי גְּשָׁמִים מַאי טִירְחָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on watering a field with rainwater on חול המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the ban is extra effort, and rainwater involves no extra effort.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree because of shadoof water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא, quoting רבי יוחנן, says rainwater was forbidden as a גזירה, so people would not confuse it with מי קילון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is a decree on rainwater because of קילון water.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: rainwater itself is not hard work, but חכמים forbade it so people would not come to use מי קילון too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer admits that rainwater involves no extra effort. The ban is a fence: people might not tell the difference between watering with collected rainwater and watering with מי קילון, so חכמים forbade both.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Because of, out of concern for

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said that Yochanan said:
It is a decree on rainwater
because of shadoof water.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה מֵי גְשָׁמִים אַטּוּ מֵי קִילוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rainwater takes no effort, so there seems to be no reason to forbid it.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden only as a protective decree because it looks like מי קילון.

steps.title: The rainwater itself will need a shadoof
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: the rainwater itself will end up needing to be lifted like מי קילון, so it really does lead to hard work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the rainwater itself will come to be קילון water.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. רב אשי says rainwater is not just a fence; it will actually turn into hard work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the rainwater can just be channeled out. Once the level in the pit drops, a person will have to lift it with a bucket, which is real טירחא. Unlike רבי יוחנן, רב אשי does not need a separate decree.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Rainwater itself
will come to be shadoof water.
phrases.notes: When the water level in the pit goes down, you'll have to haul it up with a bucket.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מֵי גְשָׁמִים גּוּפַיְיהוּ לִידֵי מֵי קִילוֹן אָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the rainwater itself will lead to hard work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the water level drops, the rainwater will need to be lifted with effort, so it is forbidden on its own terms.

steps.title: Linking the dispute to שמואל's ruling on streams from pools
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אילעא and רב אשי disagree about the ruling of רבי זירא. That ruling comes from שמואל and permits watering on חול המועד from streams fed by pools.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about the ruling of רבי זירא. For רבי זירא said that רבה בר ירמיה said that שמואל said: streams that draw water from pools may be used to water fields on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says the two answers lead to different results, and brings שמואל's ruling as the case where the difference will show.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל permits watering from a stream fed by a pool, because water from a pool will not quickly run low. How each opinion fits this ruling is not explained yet; the גמרא will spell it out next.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of a יום טוב (חול המועד)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not yet explain who agrees with שמואל and who doesn't. It only announces that the argument depends on this ruling. Step 15 spells it out.

phrases.english: And they disagree about the ruling of Rabbi Zeira.
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי אילעא and רב אשי from the last two steps.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Zeira said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: that Rabba bar Yirmeya said that Shmuel said:
Streams that draw water from pools
one is permitted to water fields from them
on the intermediate days of a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the two answers in steps 12 and 13 lead to different results, using שמואל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: streams that draw water from pools may be used for watering fields on חול המועד.

steps.title: Who accepts רבי זירא's ruling and who does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the disagreement from step 14: one אמורא accepts רבי זירא's ruling and the other does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds like רבי זירא, and one master does not hold like רבי זירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the point it started in step 14. It tells us that one of the two answers fits רבי זירא's ruling and the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said rainwater is forbidden because it will run out and you will end up lifting water. So a stream that keeps flowing is fine for him, and he agrees with רבי זירא. רבי אילעא said rainwater is forbidden because it looks like מי קילון, and that worry applies to any collected water, so he does not accept רבי זירא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Master; here it means 'one of the two Sages'
He holds of it / he accepts it
He does not hold of it / he does not accept it

phrases.english: One master holds of the ruling of Rabbi Zeira,
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי. For him the worry is only that the water runs out, and a flowing stream will not run out.

phrases.english: and one master does not hold of the ruling of Rabbi Zeira.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אילעא in the name of רבי יוחנן. For him, collected water looks like מי קילון even if it never runs out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא, וּמָר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the disagreement that step 14 announced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי accepts רבי זירא's leniency for flowing streams; רבי אילעא does not.

steps.title: רבי זירא's ruling: streams fed by pools are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes רבי זירא's ruling itself: you may water your field on חול המועד from streams that draw water from pools.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רבי זירא said in the name of רבה בר ירמיה, who said in the name of שמואל: streams that draw their water from pools may be used to water fields on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is stepping back to look at רבי זירא's ruling in full, since it was only mentioned in passing before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stream fed by a pool keeps flowing, so the farmer will not need to lift water by hand. That is why it is allowed even though it is a stream and not a natural spring.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא goes back to look closely at a statement it mentioned earlier
The middle days of the festival (חול המועד)

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabba bar Yirmeya said that Shmuel said:
streams that draw water from pools —
it is permitted to water a field from them
on the intermediate days of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ruling mentioned in steps 14 and 15 and quotes it in full.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Streams fed by pools may be used to water fields on חול המועד.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה that forbids rainwater
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא from our משנה, which forbids watering with rainwater or מי קילון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה challenged רבי זירא: But the משנה says, 'but not with rainwater and not with מי קילון'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי זירא's ruling by quoting the line of our משנה that forbids rainwater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rainwater sits in a collection and can run out, and that is why the משנה forbids it. A pool is also collected water that can run out, so a stream fed by a pool should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a source such as a משנה or ברייתא)
Rainwater collected in pits or cisterns
Water lifted up with a shadoof, a hand-worked bucket lever

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised an objection to Rabbi Zeira:
But not with rainwater
and not with water drawn with a shadoof!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's leniency for streams fed by pools
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids rainwater because collected water can run out. Pools are also collected water, so streams fed by them should be forbidden too.

steps.title: The pools of בבל never run dry
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the pools in בבל are so full that they act like water that never stops flowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: ירמיה, my son, these pools of בבל are like water that does not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. He explains that the pools שמואל was talking about are not like rainwater, because they never run out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer accepts the reason the משנה forbids rainwater, which is that it runs out. It then shows that this reason does not apply to the pools of בבל. Since they never dry up, nobody will need to lift water by hand, and the leniency stands.

keyTerms.meaning: My son, a warm way of addressing a student
They are like / they are compared to

steps.whatToRemember: Watering is allowed or forbidden based on one question: can the water run out and push you into hard work? The pools of בבל cannot run out, so the streams they feed are allowed.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yirmeya, my son,
these pools of Babylonia —
are like water that does not stop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction of cases: the pools of בבל are not like rainwater that can run out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pools are collected water like rainwater, so streams fed by them should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pools of בבל never run dry, so they count like constantly flowing water and are allowed.

steps.title: A ברייתא: pools filled before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that pools filled before יום טוב may not be used for watering on חול המועד, but if a water channel runs between them, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: temporary pools and regular pools that were filled with water before יום טוב may not be used to water fields on חול המועד. But if a water channel passes between them, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same subject: when you may and may not water from pools on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pool that was filled once can run dry, and then you would have to work hard to bring water. If a channel keeps flowing through the pools, they stay full, so the worry is gone. This matches the idea behind רבי זירא's ruling: water that keeps flowing is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; this opens a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא confirms the rule behind this whole discussion: water that can run out is forbidden, and water with a steady supply is allowed.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
temporary pools and regular pools
that were filled with water from the eve of the festival —
it is forbidden to water a field from them
on the intermediate days of the festival.
But if a water channel
was passing between them — it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that follows the same rule as רבי זירא's ruling: steady water is allowed, and water that can run out is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pools filled before יום טוב are forbidden for watering on חול המועד, unless a water channel flows between them.

steps.title: רב פפא limits the water channel permission
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the permission from the ברייתא applies only when most of the field can drink from that channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is allowed only when most of the field gets its water from that channel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a condition to the ברייתא from step 19, which allowed watering from pools when a water channel runs between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry in this whole discussion is that a person will end up working hard to bring water from somewhere else. If most of the field drinks from the channel at once, there is little left to water, so he will not rush to another source. That is why רב פפא allows it only in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only when (introduces a condition)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And this applies only when the majority of that field
drinks from that water channel.
phrases.notes: "Drinks" means gets watered. The channel is the one between the pools from step 19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the ברייתא's permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The water channel permission applies only if most of the field is watered from it.

steps.title: רב אשי allows it even for a minority of the field
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees: even if most of the field does not drink from the channel, it is allowed, because the steady flow means the owner will be patient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if most of the field does not drink from it, it is allowed. Since the water keeps flowing in, the owner tells himself: If the field doesn't get watered in one day, it will get watered over two or three days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with רב פפא and allows using the channel even when it cannot water most of the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, what matters is that the channel keeps refilling. Because the water keeps coming, the owner is calm and will not rush to work hard. The size of the watered area is not the issue.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the person may work harder. He is saying the steady flow makes the person relaxed, so the worry about effort is gone.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even though the majority
of that field does not drink from it,
since it keeps drawing water and coming,
he says to himself:
If it does not drink in one day,
let it drink over two or three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רוּבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפא's condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A steadily flowing channel may be used even if it waters only part of the field, since the owner will not rush.

steps.title: A pool that collects drips from another field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a pool collecting drips from one irrigated field may be used to water another irrigated field.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A pool that receives drips of water from this irrigated field may be used to water another irrigated field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a pool that fills from water dripping off a field that is being irrigated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper field is watered, and its extra water drips into a pool. The ברייתא allows using that pool to water a second field on חול המועד. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A pool that receives dripping water
from this field that needs irrigation
it is permitted to water from it
another field that needs irrigation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on a related case of watering sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pool fed by drips from an irrigated field may be used to water another field.

steps.title: But the dripping might stop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the drips are likely to stop, so the pool is not a reliable source.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is likely to stop!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's permission by pointing out that the dripping may stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps allowed only sources that keep flowing, because then the owner will not have to work hard to find water. Dripping from a field seems unreliable. If it stops, he may rush to bring water from elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: It is likely to (literally, it is made to)

phrases.english: But isn't it likely to stop!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא permitting watering from a drip-fed pool.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Drips are an unreliable source. When they stop, the owner will exert himself, which goes against the idea behind the other permissions.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: it is still dripping
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the field is still dripping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is talking about when it is still dripping.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to a case where the dripping continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not allow it in every case. It allows it only while the water is actively dripping into the pool, so it works like a source that keeps flowing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
And it is still trickling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: וַעֲדַיִין הִיא מְטַפְטֶפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow it even if the drips might stop.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only while the dripping continues.

steps.title: אביי: only if the first spring has not stopped
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the upper field's own spring must still be flowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And this applies only when the first spring has not stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another condition: the spring that waters the upper field must still be running.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drips only last as long as the upper field keeps getting water. So the true sign that the pool is reliable is that the original spring is still flowing. Then the drips will keep coming.

keyTerms.meaning: The first spring (the one watering the upper field)

steps.whatToRemember: A drip-fed pool may be used only while it keeps dripping, which depends on the upper field's spring still running.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And this applies only when the first spring has not stopped.
phrases.notes: The "first spring" is the one watering the upper field, whose extra water drips into the pool.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא פָּסַק מַעְיָין רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further sharpens the answer to the קשיא by naming the source of the drips.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any drip-fed pool might be unreliable.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the first spring is still flowing, the drips continue and the pool is reliable.

steps.title: No lifting water from a lower bed to a higher bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא teaches that with two garden beds, one higher than the other, you may not draw water from the lower one to water the higher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: Two garden beds, one above the other: one may not draw water from the lower one to water the upper one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about drawing water upward on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water flows down by itself, but lifting it up takes real effort. That kind of work is not allowed on חול המועד, so water may not be lifted from the lower bed to the upper one.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
Two garden beds, one above the other:
one may not draw water from the lower one
and water the upper one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new ברייתא on effort in watering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water may not be drawn from a lower bed to water a higher bed on חול המועד.

steps.title: Even within one garden bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר שמעון goes further: even in one bed with a low half and a high half, you may not lift water from the low part to the high part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even more than that, רבי אלעזר בר שמעון said: Even one garden bed, half low and half high: one may not draw water from the low place to water the high place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בר שמעון extends רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's rule to a single garden bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think one bed counts as one unit, so moving water inside it is fine. רבי אלעזר בר שמעון says no. The effort of lifting water upward is the problem, even inside the same bed.

keyTerms.meaning: Even more than that (introduces a bigger חידוש)

steps.whatToRemember: Lifting water upward is forbidden on חול המועד, whether between two beds or even inside one bed.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Furthermore, Rabbi Elazar bar Shimon said:
Even one garden bed
half of it low and half of it high:
one may not draw water from the low place
and water the high place.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the previous ruling to a stricter case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even within a single bed, water may not be lifted from a lower part to a higher part.

steps.title: A ברייתא about tending vegetables on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that one may do 'מדלין' for vegetables in order to eat them, but doing it only to make them look nicer is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may do 'מדלין' for vegetables in order to eat them. But if it is done to make them look nicer, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about caring for vegetables on חול המועד. Whether the work is allowed depends on why you are doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same action can be allowed or forbidden based on its purpose. Work done so you can eat the vegetables during the festival is permitted. Work done just to make them look better is not a real need, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
Usually understood as 'drawing water' (from דְּלִי, a bucket). Its exact meaning is debated in the next steps.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't lock in the meaning of 'מדלין' yet. The story right after this argues about what the word really means.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may 'draw' for vegetables in order to eat them,
but if it is in order to make them look nicer, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of watering and field work on חול המועד with a new ברייתא about vegetables.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מדלין for vegetables is allowed in order to eat them, but forbidden if it is only to make them look nicer.

steps.title: רבה תוספאה wants to put a man in נידוי
steps.stepSummary: While walking, רבינא and רבה תוספאה see a man drawing water with a bucket on חול המועד. רבה תוספאה tells רבינא to put him in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא and רבה תוספאה were walking on the road. They saw a man drawing water with a bucket on חול המועד. רבה תוספאה said to רבינא: Let the master come and put him in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a debate about the ברייתא we just learned. רבה תוספאה thinks the man is doing forbidden work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה תוספאה sees drawing water with a bucket on חול המועד as breaking the words of the חכמים, serious enough for נידוי. This sets up the question of whether the ברייתא allows what the man is doing.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of the festival
To put him in נידוי (שַׁמְתָּא, a ban)

phrases.english: Ravina and Rabba Tosefa'a
were walking along the road.
They saw a certain man
who was drawing water with a bucket on the intermediate days of the Festival.
Rabba Tosefa'a said to Ravina:
Let the master come and excommunicate him.
phrases.notes: 'Master' is a polite way of addressing רבינא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא וְרַבָּה תּוֹסְפָאָה הֲווֹ קָא אָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case that tests how to read the ברייתא of step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה תוספאה holds that drawing water with a bucket on חול המועד deserves נידוי.

steps.title: רבינא objects: the ברייתא allows it
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבה תוספאה from the ברייתא, which says one may do מדלין for vegetables in order to eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: But it was taught in a ברייתא: One may draw for vegetables in order to eat them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back. He cites the ברייתא from step 28 to show that the man may be doing something allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא reads 'מדלין' as drawing water to irrigate. If so, the man could be watering vegetables he plans to eat, which the ברייתא permits. So there is no reason for נידוי.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא! Used to bring a source that challenges a statement.

phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is רבינא, answering רבה תוספאה.

phrases.english: One may draw for vegetables in order to eat them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה תוספאה's call for נידוי in step 29, using the ברייתא of step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה תוספאה's view that the man deserves נידוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows drawing water for vegetables in order to eat them, so the man may be doing something permitted.

steps.title: רבה תוספאה: you misread the word מדלין
steps.stepSummary: רבה תוספאה answers that 'מדלין' in the ברייתא does not mean drawing water, and he begins to explain what it does mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think that 'מדלין' means drawing water? Rather, what does it mean... (continued in the next line).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה תוספאה defends himself by rejecting רבינא's reading of the ברייתא. The sentence breaks off here, and the real meaning is given at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's challenge only works if 'מדלין' means drawing water. רבה תוספאה rejects that reading. If the ברייתא is about some other kind of work, it gives no permission for drawing water with a bucket, so his call for נידוי stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think...? Introduces a rejection of the other person's assumption.

steps.confusionAlert: רבה תוספאה is not arguing with the ruling of the ברייתא. He is arguing about what one word in it means.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a whole practical ruling, here even נידוי, can depend on the meaning of one word in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבה תוספאה is answering רבינא.

phrases.english: Do you think that what is meant by 'madlin'
is drawing water?
Rather, what is meant by...

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ מַאי מַדְלִין מַדְלִין מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in step 30 by rejecting how he read the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא assumed 'מדלין' means drawing water to irrigate, so the man was allowed to do it.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מדלין' does not mean drawing water. The real meaning comes next, so the ברייתא does not permit the man's action.
